lawyer:

Vs.
Asifadoullah ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
This appeal at the instance of the plaintiff-appellant is directed against the judgment and decree passed by the learned 3rd Subordinate Judge, Chittagong in Partition Appeal No. 245 of 1965 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif, Putiya in Partition Suit No. 71 of 1964 decreeing the suit in part. 

 2. Plaintiff filed the suit for partition of the disputed property and allotment of saham in respect of 1/3rd share and also for purchasing the 2/3rd share of defendants 1 to 3 under section 4 of the Partition Act, 1893. The case of the plaintiff is that the disputed homestead recorded in R.S. plot No. 225 measuring .28 decimals belonged to Bijon Bihi. Bijon Bibi was survived by her son Mochad Ail and daughter Abjan Bibi who possessed the homestead after the death of Bijon Bibi. Mochad Ali died leaving defendants 8 and 9, son and daughter defendant No. 10 who were also in possession of the homestead. Abjan Bibi was survived by her son Abdul Malek who also died leaving plaintiff as his sole heir Plaintiff has therefore, 1/3rd share in the homestead and he is in possession of it. The 2/3rd share of Mochad Ali was auction purchased by Fajar Ali, the predecessor of defendants 4 to 7. Fajar Ali subsequently transferred his 2/3rd share to defendants 1 to 3. Defendants 1 to 3 are stranger to the family of the plaintiff. They are trying to dispossess the plaintiff and proforma defendants 8 to 10. Plaintiff along with proforma defendants 8 to 10 filed title suit no. 127 of 1959 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Putiya against the defendants 1 to 7 and got decree in respect of plaintiff's 1/3rd share with direction to possess the same as ejmali. Defendant 1 to 7 did not get possession in the homestead. In such circumstances if the plaintiff is not permitted to purchase their share it will be impossible on the part of the plaintiff to live in the homestead. 

 4. The learned Munsif considered the case on merit and held that plaintiff is not entitled to purchase the 2/3rd share of the defendants. So he decreed the suit in respect of the plaintiffs 1/3rd share and passed an order for partition of the disputed property accordingly. He also rejected the defendant's prayer for purchase of the 1/3d share of the plaintiffs. 

 Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court plaintiffs filed Partition Appeal No. 245 of 1965. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, plaintiff filed this appeal. 

 8. There is no dispute that plaintiff is owner to the extent of 1/3rd share in the disputed homestead. It has also been found by the lower appellate Court that plaintiff has one but in the disputed homestead. There is, therefore, no denying the fact that the plaintiff has been in possession of the homestead in part. But the main question is whether the plaintiff is a member of the family of Bijon Bibi or Mochad Ali. There does not appear any dispute that Abjan after marriage went to the house of her husband and become a member of his family and lived there in different place, Plaintiff's father Abdul Malek was also a member of his parent’s family and lived there. So also plaintiff, his father and grand-mother did not live in the house with Bijon Bibi and Mochad Ali as member of their family. In such circumstances there does not appear any error of law or procedure in the finding and the decision of the lower appellate Court. The decision referred to by the learned Advocate for the appellant does not apply with regard to the question whether he was a member of the family of Bijou Bibi or Mochad Ali On the other hand, the learned Advocate for the Respondent referred to the decision reported in 13 D.L.R. 230 in case of Khandaker Belayet Hossain vs. Ayesha Siddiquika and others and the decision in the case of Chowdhury Mohammad Ismail Khan Vs. Massammat Amirjan reported in 195 I.C. 504 in support of his contention that a female member of an undivided family who marries and goes to live in her husband's house prima facie gives up her intention of continuing to reside in her old house and so she is prima facie no longer a member of the family and as such as he is not entitled to the benefits of section 4 of the Partition Act. From the facts and circumstances of the case and the decisions referred to by the learned Advocate for the Respondent which are applicable in this case. I do not find any reason to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court.
